R1_oracle_on_e3x.note: R1 on the expansion sample is NOT 1.0000 at the certified tolerance, unlike the original sample. One structure (mp-1078353, true triclinic) reconstructs as cubic even at tau=0.01 with all 5 views and exact ray triangulation; this is a genuine identifiability failure on the second draw, not a merge-tolerance artifact, and it means Rone=1.0000 does not automatically transfer to a new sample drawn under the same protocol.

below_baseline_replication.verdict: The below-baseline claim as stated in the leaderboard figure caption -- 'every model on this draw falls below the shape-free baseline' -- is about the ORIGINAL zero-shot leaderboard (13 models, all below 0.5286) and is explicitly scoped in the manuscript text as 'specific to this draw'. That scoping is CORRECT and REPLICATES: none of the three frontier arms present on e3x falls below the e3x floor (0.2476) either -- all three clear it, by a WIDER margin than on the original sample, because the floor itself collapsed (0.5286->0.2476) while the frontier arms held. The chain arm V2b is the one case that reverses sign: below floor on original (p=1.3e-03), above floor on expansion (p=1.6e-03), pooled null (p=1.00).

R1_certified_vs_released_replication.verdict: R1=1.0000 (exact ceiling at the certified tolerance) does NOT replicate on the second draw: it is 0.9952 (209/210) on e3x. The manuscript's claim that emptiness of the phantom set (Phi_0=empty) holds 'on every one of the 1950 certified structures' is about the identifiability-certified pool used for the scale-up baselines, not about e3x directly, and this result shows the certified-emptiness property is sample-dependent rather than guaranteed to hold on an arbitrary second draw of n=210 under the same protocol.

median_share_discrepancy_reconciliation.verdict: BOTH NUMBERS ARE CORRECT ARITHMETIC on the same 14-model, same-P(m) decomposition; they differ only in which oracle value is used as R1 in the denominator and in R1-R3 for S(m). 0.2901/13-of-14 uses the certified R1=1.0000 (delta=tau=0.01, the theoretically exact ceiling established in Theorem 1's identifiability result). 0.3092/12-of-14 uses R1rel=0.9524 (the released pipeline's operating tolerance delta=0.15=15*tau). The manuscript explicitly states this choice and its effect (section_methods.tex: 'at R1rel the two rungs differ by 0.0476 and every share would shift downward, which is one practical consequence of the released tolerance'; section_results.tex explicitly reports both: 0.2901 at R1 and 12-of-14 at R1rel). This is a DEFENSIBLE, DISCLOSED, and CONSISTENT choice, not an unexplained drift: the memo's 0.3092/12-of-14 is the value at the released tolerance and the manuscript's 0.2901/13-of-14 is the value at the certified tolerance, and the manuscript reports both explicitly in the same paragraph. There is no discrepancy once the reference point is identified; the retired memo did not yet have the R1/R1rel distinction and reported only the released-tolerance number under the label 'R1', which reads as a different number from the current text's 'R1' but is arithmetically the same computation at a different oracle setting.

RF19_reproducibility_caveat.note: The 19-feature RF (not the floor) shows the SAME multi-value non-reproducibility documented in results/classifier_refreeze (0.8905 original run, 0.8857 reproduced, 0.8762 gradient boosting): my independent refit gives 0.8952 on e3 original and 0.8810 on e3x, both different again from the 0.8857/0.8667 pair reported in eval_expansion. Package versions likely differ slightly (this run: sklearn as installed in the python conda env) from the frozen classifier_specifications.json environment (sklearn 1.9.0, numpy 2.4.6). The 3-FEATURE FLOOR, which is what every below-floor test in this record depends on, reproduces EXACTLY (0.5286 original, 0.2476 expansion) across all three independent computations, so this instability does not touch the below-floor conclusions.
